swap_trigger.recheck_rule: nothing to act on: no pair clears the toll of the exchange. After execution the only number that can bring the decision back is the toll of the exchange it would have to make: re-read this face on the next decision bar, and act again only if a pair's gap exceeds 0.16 pp (2 sides x 8 bp). Getting the book back where it came from pays that same exchange once more, so the whole manoeuvre is 0.32 pp (4 sides) -- that number answers 'did the discount pay for the trip', never 'may I act'.
caveats: the trigger is priced in pp of notional and compared against the toll of ONE exchange (0.16 pp, 2 sides) only; the whole manoeuvre (0.32 pp, 4 sides) is published next to it and is never the threshold. It does not price tracking difference, fee, size or FX-hedge policy between the two tickers
episode lengths are measured on the reconstructed gap, which inherits the single IOPV anchor of the gap face; censored episodes are reported, never scored as zero
a 'window always open' reading means the pair is structurally wide, not that the swap has to be repeated: the book only has to hold it once

the merged name's share is a share of the risk book, not of NAV: it carries the same basket as the two legs it replaced, so the number of independent baskets is printed beside it and is what the concentration reading should use

swap benefits are re-scaled linearly with notional (the gap face prices them as a percentage of the traded amount); fees, tracking difference and FX-hedge policy between the two tickers are still not priced
the netted order is lot-rounded at the sibling's close on the priced bar; intraday execution will move both the proceeds and the bought lots

caveats: the reconciliation compares two documents, not two accounts: it says what the printed rows leave behind relative to the book the same face declares, and it cannot see whether the broker actually filled those lots

the base divergence holds the target weights of THIS ticket fixed on purpose -- it isolates the starting-book effect. What the next decision bar selects is a different question and is not answered here
prices are the sheet's own bar closes; a real execution will move both the share counts and the cash leg
